questions.cardText:
[Zoology] Why do tigers sometimes roar after catching their prey?
A. To invite other tigers to share
B. To warn other tigers away
C. To call their cubs
Answer: A. Though tigers are usually solitary and highly territorial, they may occasionally roar after a kill to share with other tigers, which improves their chance of survival in the future.
questions.de: Was erlaubt ein Tigermännchen, anders als ein Löwenmännchen, manchmal den Weibchen und Jungen in seinem Revier mit seiner Beute, bevor er selbst fertig ist?
questions.en: Unlike a male lion, what does a male tiger sometimes allow the females and cubs within his home range to do with his kill before he has finished with it?

timeline.labelEn: Carl Linnaeus scientifically describes the tiger
timeline.labelDe: Carl von Linné beschreibt den Tiger wissenschaftlich

questions.notes: Card's claim (tigers roar after a kill to invite others to share) is not supported: Wikipedia says tigers roar to signal their presence over long distances, during mating, and a mother roars to call her cubs (the card's option C); no source found for roaring to invite sharing. Asked instead the verified fact that tigers are social at kills and a male shares the carcass with females and cubs.

questions.cardText:
[Engineering and Inventions] Why is “bone china” called bone china?
A. To signal that it is strong and light
B. Because it contains bone
C. It was named after a Chinese town that has the word “bone” in its name
Answer: B. Bone china is made using bone ash, typically from cattle bones, which is mixed with kaolin and feldspar. This gives bone china its unique strength, whiteness, and translucency.
questions.de: Welcher Rohstoff, meist aus Rinderknochen gewonnen, gibt Knochenporzellan seinen Namen sowie seine Festigkeit, Weiße und Lichtdurchlässigkeit?
questions.en: Which raw material, typically made from cattle bones, gives bone china its name and its strength, whiteness and translucency?

timeline.labelEn: Josiah Spode develops modern bone china in Staffordshire (early 1790s)
timeline.labelDe: Josiah Spode entwickelt in Staffordshire das moderne Knochenporzellan (frühe 1790er)

questions.notes: Bone ash was already standard at the Bow porcelain factory from about 1747.
